questions.question: What is the main goal of informational writing?
choices: Explain a topic clearly using accurate information
Convince readers through unsupported opinion
Tell a fictional story
Entertain without a central focus

questions.question: Which thesis best fits an explanation of how urban trees reduce heat?
choices: Trees are wonderful
Urban trees cool neighborhoods by providing shade and releasing water vapor
This report is about cities
Some streets have trees

questions.question: A paragraph explains how a volcano forms. Which structure is most appropriate?
choices: A dialogue between fictional characters
A list of preferences
A sequence of processes and cause-and-effect relationships
A debate with no evidence

questions.question: Why should technical terms be defined for a general audience?
choices: Definitions make evidence unnecessary
Every reader already knows technical vocabulary
Terms should replace examples
Readers need enough context to understand the explanation

questions.question: Which evidence best supports an explanation of a local recycling program's results?
choices: Documented participation and material recovery data
A slogan from the program poster
One person's unrelated opinion
A photograph with no date or context

questions.question: A draft includes facts but no transitions between sections. What would help?
choices: Remove the headings
Add language that shows how the ideas connect
Add unrelated quotations
Repeat the title after each sentence

questions.question: A writer is explaining a complex process. What can a labeled diagram contribute?
choices: Proof that the process always works
A replacement for all explanations
A visual representation of parts or steps that supports the text
An unrelated opinion

questions.question: Which choice best distinguishes an example from a definition?
choices: An example is always a quotation
A definition must include a statistic
They have the same purpose
An example illustrates a concept; a definition states what it means

questions.question: A report says a new policy 'caused' attendance to rise but only compares two years. What should be improved?
choices: Consider other factors and avoid claiming causation without adequate evidence
Remove all dates
Change the topic
Add a stronger adjective

questions.question: How can a writer avoid overwhelming readers with facts?
choices: Include every fact found
Select details that directly explain the main idea and organize them clearly
Remove the main idea
Put evidence in random order

questions.question: Which paragraph order best explains how a water filter works?
choices: List parts alphabetically with no explanation
Give the conclusion before naming the process
Describe the parts, then trace water through each stage
Mix steps and unrelated facts

questions.question: What is paraphrasing in informational writing?
choices: Changing a few words and omitting attribution
Copying a source exactly
Writing an unsupported opinion
Restating source information in new wording while preserving its meaning and crediting it

questions.question: A writer compares two energy sources. What should guide the comparison?
choices: Consistent criteria such as cost, reliability, and environmental impact
Different criteria chosen for each source
Only the writer's favorite source
The length of each source's name

questions.question: Which detail is most relevant in a section about a city's water use?
choices: A famous river in another continent
Household and industrial water-use data for that city
The author's favorite drink
The history of a local sports team

questions.question: Why should an explanatory conclusion synthesize rather than introduce a new topic?
choices: A new topic makes the evidence stronger
A conclusion should not connect to the main idea
It helps readers understand the significance of the explanation they just read
Synthesis removes all details

questions.question: A writer uses a chart from a source. What must the writer do?
choices: Remove its labels
Present it as the writer's own data
Assume the chart needs no context
Identify the source and explain what the chart shows

questions.question: Which sentence is the most objective?
choices: The survey included 240 students from four grade levels
The survey was amazing
The results are obviously perfect
Everyone loved the survey

questions.question: A section contains five paragraphs on separate subtopics. What can improve navigation?
choices: Remove all paragraph breaks
Use clear headings that reflect each subtopic
Repeat the same heading everywhere
Put the conclusion in the middle

questions.question: A writer finds a reliable source, but it is ten years old. What should the writer ask?
choices: Whether old sources are always false
Whether the source has enough pages
Whether the information may have changed and needs a current source
Whether the title is interesting

questions.question: Which revision best improves clarity?
choices: Add more passive sentences
Remove key terms
Combine unrelated ideas into one sentence
Replace vague pronouns with the specific people or things they refer to
